subject: QuantifyAI pilot — traffic snapshot + guidance on GPU mix
messages:
From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
To: Jin Park <jin.park@quantify.ai>, Quantify AI Platform Ops <ops@quantify.ai>
Cc: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 22 Mar 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: QuantifyAI pilot: initial traffic snapshot request

Hi Jin / Quantify ops team,

Thanks for taking the call earlier — excited to get the pilot scoping moving. To give you a tight Dedicated estimate and a recommended GPU mix, can you send a short snapshot of the production traffic shape you expect during the 30-day pilot? The key items that help us size are below — a quick CSV or a few bullet answers is totally fine.

Ask list (minimal):
- Avg concurrent live sessions during normal hours (and during peak minute)
- Expected peak-minute RPS (inbound requests per second) and duration of the peak window (e.g., 10 min every hour / 1 hour twice per day)
- Typical prompt token length distribution (median, 90th) and average response tokens per request
- Percent of requests that are multi-turn (session affinity) vs stateless single-shot
- KV-cache hit-rate (if you plan to use prefix caching) or cache avoidance patterns
- Percent of requests that call external tools/functions (webhook calls, retrieval) and expected additional latency budget
- Any hard P99 latency requirement (ms) and acceptable fallback behavior if Dedicated capacity is saturated

If you have a token sample or small request log, you can attach it (redact user identifiers) — that helps a lot for batching and occupancy estimates. I attached a blank sizing workbook if you prefer to fill it.

I'll loop in our capacity/quant team (Mina & Vivek) once you share the snapshot and we'll return a 1-page capacity recommendation + cost sketch within 48 business hours.

Thanks,
Marcus
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
--
[Attachment: sample_sizing_workbook_template.xlsx (xlsx)]

From: Jin Park <jin.park@quantify.ai>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.com>
Cc: Quantify AI Platform Ops <ops@quantify.ai>
Date: Fri, 23 Mar 2028 11:34:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: QuantifyAI pilot: initial traffic snapshot request

Hey Marcus / Mina,

Thanks — attaching a small token sample and a one-page traffic note. High level answers below; attaching a CSV with anonymized request rows for two 24-hour windows (weekday, weekend).

Quick answers (rounded):
- Avg concurrent live sessions: 1,800 (normal) / peak concurrent: ~7,400 (peak minute during marketing blast)
- Peak-minute RPS: 125 rps sustained for ~12 minutes during peak windows; we also see repeated 90s bursts of ~60 rps across the day
- Prompt tokens: median 60; 90th pct 320; mean response tokens per request ~120
- Multi-turn: ~42% of requests are multi-turn with session affinity; avg session length ~3.2 requests
- KV cache: expected hit-rate ~28% (we currently only cache user profile prefixes)
- External function calls: ~12% of requests call our retrieval service; adds ~80-120ms on our side
- P99 latency target: 350ms end-to-end for interactive features; background batch tasks can be relaxed

Files attached: quantify_token_samples.csv (anonymized), quantify_traffic_note.pdf (short). Let me know if you need a longer window.

-Jin
Head of Platform | Quantify AI
--
[Attachment: quantify_token_samples.csv (csv)]

From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
To: Jin Park <jin.park@quantify.ai>, Quantify AI Platform Ops <ops@quantify.ai>
Cc: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 26 Mar 2028 08:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: QuantifyAI pilot: initial traffic snapshot request

Appreciate the fast turnaround, Jin — this is perfect.

Next steps from our side:
- Mina & Vivek: I uploaded Jin's CSV to the sizing workbook and ran an initial token-distribution pass. Please review the attached filled worksheet (quantifyai_sizing_workbook.xlsx) for assumptions I used (burst window = 12 min at 125 rps; KV hit-rate 28%; multi-turn session factor 1.42).
- Jin: could you confirm whether the marketing blasts are expected weekly or ad-hoc? If weekly we can recommend a burst-hardened slice with reserved burst capacity rather than full commit. Also, confirm whether you need strict data residency in us-west region.

I included a couple of specific questions where assumptions matter:
1) For multi-turn sessions, do you keep session affinity pinned to a single GPU pool, or are you okay with routing relaxed across a tenantized pool?
2) Do you expect synchronous blocking on retrieval calls (they currently add 80-120ms), or can you adopt async tool-calling (which increases queueing complexity but reduces required headroom)?

I'll ask Mina to produce two configuration sketches: (A) cost-optimized mix (higher oversubscription, more batching; likely A100-heavy) and (B) latency-optimized mix (lower oversubscription, H100 tilt + reserved burst nodes). Expect a short delivery by Tuesday EOD.

Thanks,
Marcus
--
[Attachment: quantifyai_sizing_workbook.xlsx (xlsx)]

From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
To: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 27 Mar 2028 15:04:00 -07:00
Subject: Fwd: QuantifyAI pilot: initial traffic snapshot request

FYI — forwarding Jin's traffic note and token samples. My initial read suggests two candidate proposals:

Proposal A — Cost-sensitive (pilot budget-friendly)
- GPU mix: 60% A100 40% H100 (oversubscribe to 4x on latency-tolerant tail)
- Autoscale: aggressive batching windows, prefer 2–3s batching for async endpoints
- Expected p99 (serving only): ~420–520ms under peak minute with caching; may miss 350ms requirement unless we reserve burst nodes

Proposal B — Latency-sensitive (meet 350ms p99 during peak)
- GPU mix: 25% A100 75% H100; reserved burst pool sized for peak-minute RPS
- Autoscale: short batching, more dedicated headroom, prefix caching optimized for session affinity
- Expected p99: ~320–350ms under modeled assumptions

Questions for you both:
- Can we get a quick back-of-envelope on cost delta between these (USD/month) for the pilot?
- Any recommended guardrails for safe fallback (model tier fallback, reduced response length) that are low-friction to implement?

Thanks — please add your numbers inline and I will package this for Jin tomorrow.

-Marcus
